headline: Medium risk: Haystack’s broad network/MCP surface can leak or misroute PDF-derived content into pdf.js workflows, but pdf.js is local-only and no direct shared channel is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Haystack can call MCP servers and REST APIs, so if pdf.js output is bridged into Haystack via a shared workspace or manual handoff, attacker-controlled PDF text could be treated as instructions. pdf.js itself only exposes PDF files and browser-based tests, so the interaction is inferred rather than directly documented; uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF pdf.js output is copied into a Haystack prompt or MCP input without provenance checks, injection is possible.
IF a shared filesystem or clipboard bridge is introduced, Haystack may parse PDF content as instructions.
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of raw PDF text into prompts.
Add a provenance tag to all pdf.js-derived content before Haystack reads it.
Use a separate workspace directory for each agent.
Require a human review step before any MCP call uses PDF-derived text.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction-stripping at the handoff boundary.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Haystack has broad network egress and can call REST/MCP endpoints, while pdf.js processes PDF files locally with no egress. If both touch the same PDFs or extracted text in a shared workspace, Haystack can transmit that content outward. The pairwise leak path is plausible in default deployments, but not directly evidenced, so medium fits.
conditions: IF both agents access the same PDF workspace, Haystack can exfiltrate extracted text via network calls.
IF pdf.js output is forwarded into Haystack prompts, that content may leave the local environment.
mitigations: Keep pdf.js and Haystack on separate workspaces.
Block Haystack egress except to approved endpoints.
Avoid sending full PDF text to Haystack unless necessary.
Review logs for accidental document content transmission.
requires-engineering: enforce per-document access controls and egress allowlists.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Haystack has network/MCP capabilities, but pdf.js is not runnable and only exposes PDF-file I/O plus browser-based tests. There is no documented overlapping write surface or shared mutable resource, so a direct capability conflict is unlikely. The only plausible conflict is if an operator wires both into the same workspace, which is unusual.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write into the same directory, file-level conflicts can occur.
IF an orchestrator maps shared mutable state to both agents, race conditions become possible.
mitigations: Assign distinct output directories.
Serialize any shared file writes.
Use read-only mounts for pdf.js inputs.
Check for duplicate filenames before writes.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared artifacts.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Haystack can consume external inputs through MCP/REST, so if pdf.js output is fed into it, Haystack may treat extracted text as authoritative without verification. pdf.js is a document processor, not a validator, so errors or malformed extraction can cascade into downstream Haystack outputs. The pathway exists in common workflows, but no direct action-taking authority is shown.
conditions: IF pdf.js extraction is used as the sole source for Haystack answers, extraction errors can propagate.
IF Haystack is prompted to summarize or act on pdf.js output without verification, downstream mistakes increase.
mitigations: Require a second-pass verification step for extracted text.
Show source-page references alongside summaries.
Reject low-confidence OCR or extraction outputs.
Limit Haystack to retrieval, not action-taking, on pdf.js content.
requires-engineering: add automated consistency checks between PDF text and summaries.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and touch non-sensitive classes by default: Haystack handles anonymous usage statistics, while pdf.js handles PDF documents. No residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented, so compliance risk is limited to ordinary document handling. The other agent is not cited beyond its data class because no specific compliance gap is shown.
conditions: IF PDF documents contain regulated data, the operator must classify them before processing.
IF Haystack is configured to store prompts or logs, retention policy review is needed.
mitigations: Classify PDFs before ingestion.
Disable unnecessary logging.
Set a short retention window for extracted text.
Confirm local data-handling policy for both tools.
requires-engineering: add policy-based redaction and retention controls.
